subject: medicine
title: Pericardial diseases

steps.tx: Suspect acute pericarditis when sharp **pleuritic pain** eases on sitting and leaning forward but worsens on lying back. Listen for a scratchy **pericardial rub** at the left lower sternal edge with the breath held. Expect diffuse concave **ST elevation** with PR depression on the ECG, and check troponin for myopericardial leak. Most cases are viral and benign, so treat with NSAIDs plus colchicine, tap lymphocytic fluid for suspected TB, dialyse uraemic cases, and recall Dressler syndrome weeks after infarction.
steps.say: Suspect acute pericarditis when sharp chest pain eases on sitting and leaning forward but worsens on lying back. Listen for a scratchy rub at the left lower sternal edge while the patient holds the breath. Expect diffuse concave ST elevation with PR depression on the ECG, and check troponin because a leak suggests myopericardial involvement. Most cases are viral and benign, so treat them with anti inflammatory drugs plus colchicine, tap the fluid when tuberculosis is suspected, dialyse uraemic cases, and recall Dressler syndrome that appears weeks after a heart attack.

steps.tx: This twelve lead tracing shows diffuse concave **ST elevation** with **PR depression**, the classic electrical signature of acute pericarditis. The inset marks the scratchy **pericardial rub** zone at the left lower sternal border heard best leaning forward. Learn this pattern because the exam contrasts it with infarction, where ST elevation stays localised to one territory with reciprocal change.
steps.say: Study this twelve lead tracing because it shows the classic electrical signature of acute pericarditis. Diffuse concave ST elevation spreads across many leads while the PR segment dips downward. The inset marks the scratchy rub zone at the left lower sternal border, heard best when the patient leans forward. Learn this pattern well because the exam contrasts it with infarction, where ST elevation stays localised to one territory with reciprocal change.

steps.tx: Suspect pericardial effusion when the ECG shows **low voltage** complexes and the chest film shows a **water bottle** silhouette. Confirm it with **echocardiography**, which shows an echo free space swinging around the heart. Consider TB, malignancy, uraemia and hypothyroidism as causes, tap fluid for diagnosis and relief, send cytology for malignant cells, expect milky fluid in chylopericardium, and arrange dialysis when uraemic fluid resists drugs.
steps.say: Suspect pericardial effusion when the ECG shows tiny low voltage complexes and the chest film shows a water bottle silhouette. Confirm the diagnosis with echocardiography, which shows an echo free space swinging around the heart. Consider tuberculosis, malignancy, uraemia and hypothyroidism as causes, tap fluid for diagnosis and relief, send cytology for malignant cells, expect milky fluid in chylopericardium, and arrange dialysis when uraemic fluid resists drugs.

steps.tx: Recognise cardiac tamponade from **Beck triad** of low blood pressure, raised neck veins and muffled heart sounds, with fast thready pulse. Expect a **paradoxical pulse** that falls by ten on inspiration and a Kussmaul rise in neck veins. Confirm it with **echocardiography** showing right atrial collapse with a full inferior vena cava. Give fluids to buy filling time, drain by pericardiocentesis, avoid positive pressure ventilation, and separate tension pneumothorax and right ventricular infarction that mimic it.
steps.say: Recognise cardiac tamponade from low blood pressure with raised neck veins and muffled heart sounds, plus a fast thready pulse. Expect the pulse to fall on inspiration and watch the neck veins rise further on inspiration. Confirm the diagnosis with echocardiography, which shows the right atrium collapsing with a full inferior vena cava. Give fluids to buy filling time, drain the sac by pericardiocentesis, avoid positive pressure ventilation, and separate tension pneumothorax and right ventricular infarction that mimic tamponade.

steps.tx: Suspect constrictive pericarditis when neck veins rise on inspiration in **Kussmaul sign** with an early diastolic knock. Expect **calcified shell** rings on imaging with septal bounce on breathing, and square root dips on catheter traces. Treat it with **pericardiectomy** that strips the shell, use diuretics cautiously without dropping preload, remember TB as the commonest worldwide cause, expect congested liver with ascites and low protein, and follow the patient with yearly echocardiography.
steps.say: Suspect constrictive pericarditis when the neck veins rise on inspiration with an early diastolic knock. Expect calcified rings on imaging with the septum bouncing on breathing, and square root dips on catheter traces. Treat the disease with surgery that strips the shell from the heart, use diuretics cautiously without dropping preload, remember tuberculosis as the commonest worldwide cause, expect a congested liver with ascites and low protein, and follow the patient with yearly echocardiography.
